description: seal-til-block v0 tamper-evidence (SPEC §7.6, invariant #4). The seal block rides INSIDE the encrypted ChatBody, so it is committed in the AEAD ciphertext, which is committed in the envelope id, which is device-Schnorr-signed (§4.1). Changing any seal field — here unlock_block — changes the canonical ChatBody bytes, hence their SHA-256, hence (after sealing) the envelope id and the signature over it. A recipient that re-derives the id therefore detects any tamper. Demonstrated on the plaintext ChatBody layer with two bodies differing ONLY in seal.unlock_block.
notes: SHA-256 over the UTF-8 ChatBody bytes. In the live envelope these bytes are AES-GCM-sealed and the ciphertext is committed in the content-addressed envelope id; flipping unlock_block by one block produces a different id and breaks the device signature. This is the same integrity posture as the pay-to-reach postage carrier (SPEC §6.2): the seal is in the ciphertext, not a separately-mutable plaintext field. The spec-pure path (§7.1, committed top-level seal field via a lock-core bump, vectors vc03/vc04) is the named upgrade target.
